problem: Decide per message whether to answer, call a tool, or start a deep run, cheaply and correctly
ideal: Cheapest route that still gets the right outcome; never a deep run for a question
metric: The router's whole job over the classification cases, a share held out: route (answer, tool, deep, confirm, clarify), the tool, the arguments it fills in, every tool of a multi-step request, no confirming argument on a first destructive ask, no tool call where no change was asked
gap: The pre-route fronting the planner (pre_route_then_planner) ties the planner on the whole job and costs no less, so the planner stays selected. single_prompt (the cheap call alone, declared an ablation) scores well on labels but returns a label and tool calls, not a decision: it cannot gather evidence, brief a deep run or ground an answer, so it is ranked and never a candidate. Measured planner failures: a paraphrased current-state update sent to deep or answered, and a mass destructive request sent to deep without a confirm.
action: Teach the planner to confirm before sending a destructive request to deep and to read "where I am now" as a current-state update, then re-run classification for every arm. Numbers live in results.csv; evaluation/components/leaderboard.py ranks them.

problem: Carry out a requested change to a quest (goals, notes, experiments) with the right tool and no unrequested writes
ideal: Final quest state matches the request exactly
selected_by: core/selection_table.py operate-a-quest (default pre_route; RunnerConfig.selections overrides); quest-backend passes no pre-router and is unchanged
metric: In-memory quest state after the run over the quest_ops cases, a share held out: the right tool with the right arguments, every step of a multi-step request, no write on an ambiguous or sharing message, an unconfirmed delete leaves the experiment in place, no unrequested write
gap: orchestrator_pre_route (the brain with a cheap pre-route that settles a clear request for a direct tool, ToolSpec.direct) is selected: it passes more cases than the planner path alone, at fewer model calls and lower cost, but the margin is a single case (the planner path once confirmed a delete on the first ask), so it is within run-to-run noise. direct_tool_call (the direct path alone, declared an ablation) is the cost floor: it cannot read, answer or start a deep run, so it is never a candidate. route-a-message shows the same pre-route tying the planner on routing, so the default is chosen by the outcome metric here.
action: Add duplicate-on-record and follow-up ("do it") cases, then re-run both arms several times to see whether the margin holds; widen ToolSpec.direct only to tools whose every argument the message supplies.

problem: Read targeted sources (files, DBs, Notion, Drive, Chat, MCP, Quest) for the planner
ideal: Relevant evidence within a read budget, failing soft
metric: Complete retrieval stacks only: recall@3 of the right document, and its answer readable, over 21 questions on a synthetic handbook (live adapters, fake network edge only); the composite stack is ranked against its floor. The per-source adapters are complementary sources, not alternatives, so they run as an invariant arm (evaluation/components/retrieval_sources: same questions, policy and scorer, listed but never ranked)
metric_command: evaluation/components/run.py retrieval --impl composite; evaluation/components/run.py retrieval_sources --impl files_adapter
gap: The leaderboard holds one real stack and a floor, so it cannot yet show a better stack. Not driven offline: quest_retrieval_adapter (it is keyed by goal and quest ids against the Quest API, not by a question; pinned by tests/test_quest_retrieval_decisions.py). In the per-source arm the MCP result measures plumbing (the server does the search), Drive has no search so its policy is list and read every file, and Notion locates by row (title and properties) only. Fixtures are written, not recorded, and the policy is a plain keyword gather, so a paraphrase is a miss for every source.
action: Build a second complete stack (the composite over more members, or a different merge) so the stack ranking has a challenger; add a quest_retrieval impl behind a fake QuestClient when it gains a question-keyed search; add harder cases (many same-term distractors, larger folders).

problem: Answer from the live web with bounded, cached, SSRF-safe fetches
ideal: Right passage per query at lowest search spend
metric: Live run of scripts/web_search_bench.py through the production adapter built from the environment (evaluation/components/web_search_live): an answer phrase in the observation the planner would see over public factual questions, real backend calls, latency and tokens added, with search spend at the list price per call. Invariant arm (evaluation/components/web_search): 15 fixture queries through each backend (serper, brave, tavily, searxng) and the fallback chain prove identical handling offline
metric_command: evaluation/components/run.py web_search_live --impl web_research; evaluation/components/run.py web_search --impl fallback_chain
gap: The live arm exercises only the backends configured in the environment, so the vendors that are not configured (serper, brave, tavily, searxng) have not been measured live, and the list price per call is an assumption to confirm against the vendor. The fixture payloads are written in each vendor's response shape, not recorded, so they prove handling, not relevance or freshness. The backends are this solution's implementations (the search-backends row was merged into it).
action: Run web_search_live for each vendor as its key is configured and compare spend per right answer to settle the backend; grow the live cases to the next rung of the ladder before treating a choice as settled.

problem: Run plan/answer calls on the right vendor and tier, retrying transient errors
ideal: Cheapest tier that passes the task; vendor swappable by config
metric: routing, tier fallback, retry, cost and pricing arithmetic on 56 offline cases (fake and dry-run providers)
gap: multi_provider scores 54/56 against 19/56 for a single flat provider. Two known gaps: pricing.py prices claude-opus-4 and claude-opus-4-8 at $3 per million input tokens while its family rule prices opus at $15, so the quality tier looks as cheap as balanced (MPR-080, MPR-101). The table is input tokens only. No live latency or pass rate per tier is recorded: that needs real calls at each tier.
action: Correct the opus rows in pricing.py from the current Anthropic price list; sweep QAR_EVAL_MODEL over the classification and quest_ops components per tier when spend is approved.

problem: Do bounded autonomous work to a written done-standard
ideal: Goal met within turn and cost budget; cheapest runner that can do the edit

The production reviewer's accuracy on the 39 logs (deep_review live_reviewer, 39 claude -p calls) is not recorded.
action: Run deep_review --impl live_reviewer --record where the CLI is approved to run; it must keep zero false stops.

problem: Land a bounded, backed-up file write
ideal: No write outside the configured root; every write reversible
metric: 20 offline cases on a scratch tree: ordinary create and overwrite, traversal, absolute and sibling-prefix paths, symlink escape, protected names, size and create limits, reversible overwrite (outside untouched, backup kept)
gap: files_writer 20/20 against 6/20 for a naive open-and-write floor. Binary-extension and secret-name lists are fixed in code; no case for concurrent writers.

ideal: Exactly the requested mutation, once
metric: 15 offline cases with a fake MCP client: exact tool and args once, aliased and bare names, write allowlist refusals with zero server calls, server error and dead connection, discovery
gap: mcp_write_adapter 15/15 against 3/15 for an allowlist-free passthrough floor. Real MCP servers are not exercised; the fake is at the client seam.

problem: Surface a human-only decision and stop
ideal: Every confirm reaches a person with enough detail to decide
metric: 15 offline cases with a fake Quest client: assignee fallback chain and never an unaddressed ask, kind, hold or proceed default, deadline, review link, team routing, duplicate open asks, backend failure
gap: quest_decision_sink 15/15 against 5/15 for a file-everything floor. Measures delivery and detail, not whether the brain chose to confirm instead of act (that is route-a-message).

problem: Decide what a user sees while work runs, by mode
ideal: Live shows everything; background shows only milestones
metric: 14 offline cases: LIVE shows every event in order, BACKGROUND shows only result, decision, milestone, context, tokens and done, mid-run detach, broken stream or callback
gap: progress_sinks 14/14 against 4/14 for a show-everything floor. Scores the sinks, not which events the orchestrator emits.

problem: Read and reopen past conversations as context
ideal: Right prior turn recalled, nothing leaked across users
metric: the labelled past conversation is among the three returned and no other user's conversation is, over 10 synthetic cases
gap: Only related_slices is driven (current_slice, filters and any database-backed ConversationStore are not); ClaudeConversationsAdapter (the RetrievalAdapter over the same files) is not driven. One case pins a paraphrase gap (CNV-010).
action: Add current_slice and time_range cases; add an impl per ConversationStore backend.

problem: Choose the context cards that enter a prompt
ideal: Right files in the top 3 at the lowest token cost
metric: top-1 / top-3 routing over the context_selection tasks on the current tree (symptom, paraphrase and hard shapes, a share held out), zero model calls. Outcome arm (evaluation/components/card_quality): after cards are learned from three finished tasks, a new query selects the right collection with its references resolved fresh, without spraying every card or leaking an unrelated one
metric_command: evaluation/components/run.py context_selection --impl hybrid_union; evaluation/components/run.py card_quality --impl seeded_keyword_store
gap: The live fusion now orders the union by relevance (reciprocal-rank fusion of the arms, vector rank counted at half weight, ranking in card_ids and card_metadata; rendered text keeps its stable order for prompt caching). On the grown task set the hybrid ties the keyword arm alone on strict top 3 and the semantic arm alone is worse: the vector arm adds recall only past the third card, never rank. A tie is not a win, so no measured advantage justifies the vector arm on this proxy. The embedder here is the small local one, not the production embedder, and the tasks are synthetic.
action: Run the same tasks with the production embedder and real misrouted tasks before dropping or keeping the vector arm; until then hybrid stays selected (it is the only arm that can recover a paraphrase) with the keyword arm as the cheaper equal. Measure the consolidating model pass once a model is available.

problem: Store and sync context cards across file, vector and Quest backends
ideal: No lost or duplicated cards; same behaviour on every backend
metric: One conformance case set through the CardRepository port on the filesystem, embedded Qdrant and Quest API (fake card API) backends: roundtrip, overwrite, no loss at volume and across pages, no duplicate, delete (also after restart), concurrent writers, restart, change stamp, tolerance. Every case must hold on every backend
gap: The embedded Qdrant repository returns only the first part of a large collection (load_all stops at a scan cap), so cards beyond it are silently missing from a listing; the case that pins it fails on that backend. A Qdrant server and the live Quest API are not driven; the fake follows the documented contract. Card selection quality is no longer this solution's metric (it moved to select-context as the card_quality outcome arm).
action: Make QdrantCardRepository.load_all follow every page (lift the scan cap or warn when it truncates), then re-run persist_cards; run the same cases against a Qdrant server and the dev Quest API when available.

problem: Semantic search over cards
ideal: Recall at fixed latency
metric: Labelled card in the top 3 over 16 questions (12 paraphrases) on the synthetic handbook, live embedded QdrantVectorStore, and query latency (p50 and p95 milliseconds, each within the cap written in the case data) at a fixed corpus size with deterministic filler cards; the query is embedded by the model for real
gap: The embedder is the local bge-small model, not the deployed one, and the latency is of the embedded local store on this host, not a Qdrant server over a network; a card is embedded from its first 2000 characters, so VEC-012 (the answer is at the end of a long card) misses. The latency caps are an interactive budget stated in the case, and results.csv has no latency column (the p50 and p95 are in the run output and its json).
action: Grow the card set; add a second VectorStore as an impl when one exists; measure latency against a Qdrant server at the same corpus size.

problem: Turn human corrections into reusable guidance cards
ideal: Same correction is never needed twice
metric: repeat-correction rate on 16 synthetic feedback sequences: after a correction is stored through the live ledger, does the guidance shown to the next relevant turn contain it (recall), and are corrections that do not bear on the turn kept out (precision). One component, feedback_loop, serves this row and store-feedback (many-to-one)
gap: Recorded 2026-10-16: ledger_guidance 12/16 (corrections surfaced when relevant 16/16, irrelevant kept out 7/14) vs dump_all 8/16 and no_memory 4/16. The guidance provider has no relevance cut below the card limit (no vector store or model filter in the offline arm), so a stored rule that does not bear on a turn is shown while the limit has room (FL-06, FL-09, FL-10, FL-16 pin that).
action: Rank stored rules by relevance so an unrelated rule is not shown while the card limit has room (vector or model filter, then re-run feedback_loop); a live arm with the model filter on is not recorded.

problem: Hold a live two-way chat over an external channel
ideal: Messages delivered once, in order
metric: 20 offline cases with a fake MCP gateway: ordered inbound messages, key-spelling drift, non-message and malformed events, wire failure and dead gateway, long-poll clamp, attachments, send args and ids, allowed tools only, close
gap: openclaw_channel 20/20 against 5/20 for a raw gateway-call floor. The payload shapes are tolerant guesses (no live gateway was available), so the number is conformance to those shapes; there is still one channel.
action: Record a fixture from a real gateway when one is available; add a second channel as a second impl.

problem: Skip the context search for an operation already worked out once
ideal: Same result as the slow path at a fraction of the cost
metric: fast-path hit rate and parity, offline arm with a deterministic rule model: 30 cases (right tool and args on a repeat, no lookalike write on a near miss, no tool on chat), share answered by a replayed recipe, model calls vs the planner-only path
gap: Recorded 2026-10-16 offline: recipe_replay_offline 30/30, 20 of 30 answered by a replayed recipe, 47 model calls, vs planner_only_offline 30/30 with 62 calls (24% fewer). The rule model was written with the cases in view, so this proves the replay engine (nominate, fill-args, mutating guard, learning), not a real model's judgment; the live arm (recipe_replay, planner_only through the claude CLI) is built but not recorded.
action: Run recipe_replay and planner_only with --record where the claude CLI is approved to run, and compare hit rate and cost against the offline arm.

problem: Intervene in a run only when it drifts
ideal: Few interventions, each correct
metric: digest evidence on 16 hand-labelled scenarios (contrast pairs), offline; signal match in a live arm; signal parsing and degrade-to-proceed in judges
gap: The digest shows the evidence each label depends on (offline). The signal match itself needs a model (live_model arm) and is not recorded. The digest sheds history operations first and prior escalations last, so the refusal rule keeps its evidence.
action: Record the overseer_signals live_model arm once a model spend is approved.

problem: Know which context cards no longer match their files
ideal: Every changed or deleted file is flagged, no unchanged file is
metric: precision and recall over 6 synthetic mutation cases, zero model calls
gap: The sha check reports an edited file and a deleted file. It misses one case on purpose: an edit that restores the mtime and size is trusted as unchanged (a speed trade for the mtime fast path).
action: Decide whether an mtime-preserving edit is acceptable; if not, hash on every check at a cost in speed.

problem: Put the right context into each prompt without exceeding the model limit or duplicating blocks

gap: The window and prices are read from the code that owns them, but the shares of the window and the dollar caps are policy stated in budget_inputs.json for a human to confirm. The fixtures are generated filler at sizes measured in an incident, not real content. Right-context quality (the prompt holding what the task needs) is measured by select-context and gather-evidence, not here.
action: Confirm the shares and dollar caps in budget_inputs.json; add production-sized fixtures from the private tracker.

problem: Pick the cheapest model that can do the work, and wait instead of failing when the provider or the allowance is out
ideal: The planner's difficulty rating picks the starting rung, a family name resolves to the newest live release, an operator pin always wins, an exhausted tier falls to the next cheaper one, and an outage or usage limit is recognised and resumed after its reset
metric: 42 offline cases: deep starting rung per difficulty and ladder (synonyms, unknown rating, off-ladder start, operator mapping), family resolution to the newest live id, tier resolution with and without live models and pins, lower-tier fallback, vision capability, outage wording, usage-limit detection and reset parsing; zero model calls
gap: Measures that the right model is chosen, not that the choice was the cheapest one that still succeeded; that needs live runs (route_a_message and the qualitative eval).
action: Record a cost-per-success arm once a live model spend is approved.

problem: Know what a run will cost before it spends, stop at a daily token budget, and stop taking work when the host is overloaded
ideal: Per-model prices are right (unknown models fall back to a stated default), the daily budget survives a restart and resets each day, and an overloaded host pauses pickup with hysteresis instead of flapping
selected_by: runner/poller.py (ResourceGuard, DailyUsageTracker) and cli_context bootstrap estimate
metric: 39 offline cases: price per provider and model (including unknown model and provider), bootstrap cost estimate, provider detection from the environment, daily budget (limit, off, bad value, negative tokens, restart reload), and resource-guard hysteresis for memory, free memory and load; zero model calls
gap: Prices are a hand-kept snapshot of list prices (input tokens only), so a provider price change is not noticed until the table is edited.
action: Review the price table whenever a provider announces a change; add output-token pricing if cost reporting needs it.

problem: Know on every change that the offline test suite is still whole, without running all of it: running every test is slow, parts of the suite reach real model providers, and a full run has already been killed for spend
ideal: Every test file imports and collects, no test silently disappears, and no test file passes the size ceiling without a waiver, found in under a minute with no model call
selected_by: CLAUDE.md pre-commit rule: run only the tests your change touches; this collection check is the cheap whole-suite gate
metric: pytest --collect-only over all test files in 21 shards (zero collection errors, collected count at least 97 percent of the recorded count), every test file in a shard, no unwaived oversize file, and 6 seeded broken or clean synthetic test folders; no test body runs; zero model calls
gap: Collection proves tests import and parametrise, not that they pass or that they stay offline; a missing fixture only fails at setup. The syntax-only baseline passes 10 of 29 cases.
action: Run the tests a change touches, file by file, as CLAUDE.md says. Raise the shard floors when the suite grows by re-recording.

problem: Keep a public repository free of secrets, real machine paths, object ids and real addresses, so nothing consumer specific or secret is ever published
ideal: A planted secret of any known kind is found before commit, a documented placeholder is never flagged, and the repository itself scans clean
metric: 35 offline cases: 12 planted secrets assembled from fragments (keys, tokens, private key block, home paths, object id, address), 11 documented placeholders that must stay quiet, the repository clean in 6 file groups, 6 command runs in a throwaway git repo; zero model calls
gap: The scan reads working files only, not git history, and knows the secret shapes written into hygiene.py: a vendor token with a new shape passes until a pattern and a planted case are added. The old grep one-liner baseline passes 6 of 35.
action: Add a pattern and a planted case together when a new credential shape appears.

problem: Switch which implementation serves a solution (model provider, deep runner, search backend) without editing code, and fail loudly on a typo
ideal: A name, a config override or the table default picks the class, in that order; a typo raises with the choices; every table entry imports; a config change switches the live implementation
metric: 36 offline cases (8 held out): resolve by name, override and default, loud typo, table integrity, and the live model-provider, deep-runner and search-backend sites switched by data; zero model calls
gap: A typo in [selections] for run-deep-work does not raise: resolve_deep_runner degrades to no deep runner (case SEL-034 pins it). Only three live call sites are driven.
action: Decide whether a mistyped selections value should fail at startup instead of silently disabling deep work; add a site case when a new call site consumes the table.

problem: Decide which implementation of a solution is best from recorded numbers that cannot be mis-compared or mis-recorded
ideal: The winner has the higher pass rate (equal rate: lower cost), rows on different case files are never compared, rows without provenance are flagged, a tie is not a win, every record carries the commit and the case file hash, and a call budget aborts a run
metric: 31 offline cases (9 held out) driving the live leaderboard, record_result and run_component on synthetic tables and a mini component in a throwaway git repository: winner, tie, cases_sha, unverified, git_sha, budgets, offline validity; zero model calls
gap: Synthetic tables only: it does not check that the committed results.csv is itself consistent (check_structure S16 does).
action: Add a case whenever the leaderboard or record format gains a rule.

problem: Let a newcomer or an AI learn QAR from its documents: every link works, every document is reachable from the index, every environment variable, subcommand and public name is explained, and the house voice holds
ideal: Every generated documentation case passes: no broken link, no orphan document, nothing undocumented, no em dash
metric: 452 offline cases generated from the repo by generate_cases.py: relative links and em dashes per document, index coverage, docs named by each component row, a described row per environment variable, each CLI subcommand and public name documented, and a coverage case that fails when a document or variable has no case; zero model calls
gap: 39 of 68 documents contain em dashes, against the house voice rule (39 failing cases of 452).
action: Rewrite the em dashes in the 39 documents with commas, colons or two sentences, by hand per document (a mechanical replacement changes meaning), then re-record.

problem: The anticipation engine must keep what it learned (recurring-ask patterns, live predictions with precomputed views, an outcome log) across turns and restarts, per scope, without leaking between scopes
ideal: Whatever backs the PredictionStore port returns exactly what was saved, never leaks between scopes, drops expired predictions, survives a restart and never raises
metric: share of 12 persistence contract scenarios (roundtrip, isolation, replace, expiry, view, clear, log, restart, tolerance) the store passes; 3 held out
gap: The in-memory reference fails the restart scenario by design; a consumer-side database store (quest-backend) is not scored here
action: Run the same scenarios against the consumer store through the port when it publishes one
